page: Microsoft Azure E128-64ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz, utilizing 32 physical cores configured with two threads per core to deliver 64 dedicated vCPUs. Based on the x86_64 architecture, the processor includes support for AVX-512 instructions such as AVX-512 VNNI and BF16, alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI. The server provides 1024 GB of total system RAM, establishing an allocation of 16 GB per vCPU. No discrete graphics processors are included in this configuration.

Local persistent scratch capacity is provided by 7559 GB of bundled NVMe SSD storage. Benchmark results place this instance in the top tier for Geekbench single-core (2891.0) and multi-core (26776.0) metrics, as well as PassMark CPU operations (94640.85). Large-block uncached memory throughput reaches 206.52 GB/sec for read tasks and 133.04 GB/sec for write tasks. Database benchmark operations achieve top-decile ratings, reinforced by Redis processing performance exceeding 101 million SET operations per second.

The 16:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio offers a cost-effective resource model for workloads that require large RAM capacities without incurring the software licensing costs associated with higher core counts. This instance configuration is suitable for large-scale in-memory databases, distributed memory caches, enterprise data warehousing, and intensive data processing pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E128-64ads_v7 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs and 32 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at 4.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 1024 GB of system RAM, offering an expansive 16 GB per vCPU, paired with 7559 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage. Discrete GPUs are not bundled. The x86_64 processor architecture includes AVX-512 and hardware cryptographic instructions, driving top-tier performance in PassMark CPU evaluations, Geekbench single-core and multi-core suites, and compression operations. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measures 206.52 GB/sec. This combination of vast memory capacity, substantial local NVMe disk space, and constrained core licensing exposure makes the instance well suited for memory-intensive workloads, including enterprise in-memory databases, Redis key-value clusters, extract-transform-load jobs, and high-throughput data analytics.
